The holiday reading challenge
How
the
challenge
works
Four weeks, four Jurassic English stories, ten to ﬁfteen minutes a day. Your child reads one story each week in
the free online reader at books.jurassicenglish.com (pictures, read-to-me audio and a question on every
page), then does the three activities for that story from this book.
Week Story Level Read
it
at

Inside
Level 1 (ages 4–8) books.jurassicenglish.com/book.html#kim-
and-the-thunder-inside
2 Not Now, Rosa! Level 1 (ages 5–8) books.jurassicenglish.com/book.html#not-
now-rosa
3 The Bell That Rang
Too Early
Level 2 (ages 8–10) books.jurassicenglish.com/book.html#the-
bell-that-rang-too-early
4 Mango, the Market
Cat
Level 2 (ages 8–10) books.jurassicenglish.com/book.html#mango-
the-market-cat
Younger children can do Weeks 1–2 twice; older children can start at Week 3 and repeat Weeks 1–2 as a warm-
up.
Each
week,
day
by
day
Day What
to
do About
Monday Read the whole story together in the
online reader. Answer the question on
each page.
15 minutes
Tuesday Word
fossils: dig up six words and
use them.
10 minutes
Wednesday Read the story again. Put
the
story
in
order.
10 minutes
Thursday Think
it
through: four questions, talk
ﬁrst, then write or draw.
15 minutes
Friday Read it a last time, aloud. I
can check
and ﬁll in the reading log.
10 minutes
One
rule
for
grown-ups: ask "Why do you think so?" every day. A reason from the story is worth more than a
right answer.

Think
it
through
Four questions, one for each step of the Jurassic Thinking Cycle. Talk ﬁrst, then write or draw.
Analyze:
look
closely. How do you know Kim is very angry? Find the clue on this page.
Evaluate:
what
matters
most?. Kim talks to Ben. Is that a safe choice or a wild choice?
Justify:
say
why. Tell why. Use because. You can say it, point or write.
I think it is a safe choice because .
I am not sure because .
Reﬂect:
what
did
I
learn?. What helps you feel calm when you feel angry? Draw or tell.
